messages:
Sam (Support): priya from NOVA opened a ticket: embeddings are returning vectors of varying lengths and sudden throughput collapse. reported region is us-east-1. attaching logs from their side.

Priya (Customer): Our service calls https://api.redwood-inference.us-east-1.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings using model=embed-pro-2. Since 2025-11-02T14:05Z we started seeing some responses with length=1024 but we expect 2048. Throughput fell from ~250 req/s to ~20 req/s and p95 latency jumped to ~1.9s. No code changes on our side.

Sam (Support): Copying PRI. Repro steps provided by customer:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.us-east-1.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-pro-2","input":["x"],"batch_size":64}'
```
They see intermittent 200 returns with vector_len=2048 and others with 1024. Also occasional 503s during bursts.

router-bot: Trace r-ccf9a: request arrived at edge us-east-1 -> region decision: fallback_to_nearest: ap-southeast-1 (due to us-east saturated) -> assigned pool: hosted-ap-southeast1-emb-03 -> variant: embed-pro-2.quant1024 -> cold_start=true -> worker_start_ms=820 -> vector_dim=1024 -> latency_ms=1525

Diego (Eng-ML): This looks like classic spillover to a quantized variant in another region. embed-pro-2 has two serving variants: embed-pro-2.fp16 (2048 dims) and embed-pro-2.quant (1024 dims). The client expects fp16 output. Our router shouldn't return a diff-dim variant w/o explicit permission.

Nora (Eng-Platform): Checking routing events: us-east reserved pools hit 98% around 14:03Z due to a big tenant run. Router policy threshold was breached and we allowed cross-region fallback. That produced cold starts and variant swaps. I'll pull the timeline and pool IDs.

Liam (SRE): I confirm a burst from tenant-9 at 14:02 caused the reserved autoscaler to lag. There was a 40s window where traffic overflowed to hosted fallback groups in ap-southeast. Action INF-8004 created.

Sam (Support): Priya - quick mitigation: can you try pinning explicit variant or reduce batch_size? Also capturing response headers will help (X-Assigned-Pool, X-Model-Variant, X-Routing-Trace).

Priya (Customer): Will try now. Two questions: 1) does pinning reduce our ability to burst? 2) are we billed extra when requests hit fallback region?

Diego (Eng-ML): 1) Pinning to embed-pro-2.fp16 forces same-dim variant; if that variant's pool is full you'll get 429 instead of silent dim mismatch. So you might see rejections but not mixed vectors. 2) If requests route to hosted fallback, billing is per-execution on whichever pool handles it. If client retries on 503 without idempotency we may double-bill — we'll coordinate with billing.

Sam (Support): Example curl to pin region + variant:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.us-east-1.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Region: us-east-1" \
  -H "X-Model-Variant: embed-pro-2.fp16" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-pro-2.fp16","input":["one","two"],"batch_size":16}'
```
This should keep vectors consistent. Also try batch_size 8-16 to reduce cold-start wait.

Priya (Customer): I ran the pinned call. For a small sample, all responses had 2048 dims now. Latency better. Still seeing a few 1024s earlier, but not now.

router-bot: Post-change trace r-dda3f: region resolved: us-east-1 -> assigned_pool: reserved-us-east-emb-01 -> variant: embed-pro-2.fp16 -> cold_start=false -> latency_ms=220 -> vector_dim=2048

Nora (Eng-Platform): Interim platform actions:
- increased desired replicas for reserved-us-east-emb by +3 (deployed)
- lowered fallback_threshold from 0.95 to 0.98 (temporary) to reduce spillover
- monitoring rule added: detect mixed-dimension responses per-account >0.1% -> page on first op.
INF-8004 updated with timestamps.

Liam (SRE): Longer term: autoscaler tuning and warm-pool strategy for embeddings to avoid cold starts when a tenant spikes batch workloads. I'll coordinate with infra infra-team.

Finance (Billing): If there are duplicate charges from automatic retries between 14:00-14:10Z for acct-nova, we'll reconcile and can credit confirmed duplicates. Please send request IDs for affected calls.

Diego (Eng-ML): Runtime change to avoid silent dim mismatch: adding header support X-Expected-Embedding-Dim (client optional). If header present and returned dim != expected, server will respond 409 Conflict with JSON explaining expected vs actual and X-Assigned-Pool info. This is targeted for next patch.

Sam (Support): Priya, thanks for testing pinning. Can you capture any responses that show 1024 dims after we pushed the replica increase? If you see any, include X-Assigned-Pool and X-Routing-Trace. Also, if you want, we can temporarily whitelist your account for burst_capacity to avoid future spillovers while we tune autoscaler.

Priya (Customer): Please enable burst_capacity for acct-nova if possible, that would help. Also I'll send a list of a few request IDs that look duplicated.

Nora (Eng-Platform): Burst capacity enabled for acct-nova as a temporary measure. We'll monitor for cost impact.

Sam (Support): Wrapping up: actions done and planned:
- customer pinned variant and saw improvement
- increased replicas + routing threshold tweak done
- burst_capacity enabled for customer
- runtime will add strict-dim header behavior (diego)
- autoscaler/warm-pool follow-up for INF-8004 (liam)
- billing to reconcile duplicates (Finance)

Priya (Customer): Thanks team, latency much better and dims consistent. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:

Sam (Support): Closing note: we'll leave INF-8004 open until warm-pool and autoscaler changes are merged. If Priya sees any recurrence, reopen thread with headers attached. :white_check_mark:
